CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for management of rash.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient reports a small amount of residual rash on bilateral medial cheeks. She was initially prescribed doxycycline twice daily and noted significant improvement over the first two weeks. She then reduced to once daily based on pharmacist recommendation, but reports the rash has plateaued and is not continuing to improve. Currently using sulfacetamide wash twice daily and metro cream applied after face wash. She has not been using elidel cream due to concerns after reading about the medication. Patient denies using additional cleansers or lotions. She reports feeling sun sensitive and uses protective measures including wearing a hat. She is not currently breastfeeding.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies dryness from sulfacetamide wash. Reports feeling good after using current products and notes some moisture returning.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Perioral dermatitis
Rosacea, including ocular rosacea

MEDICATIONS
Sulfacetamide wash twice daily
Metro cream applied after face wash
Doxycycline (initially twice daily, reduced to once daily)

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Not currently breastfeeding. Uses sun protection measures including hat and avoids sun exposure due to feeling sun sensitive.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Fitzpatrick skin type IV to V. Bilateral medial cheeks show a few faint erythematous papules with minimal redness around and underneath nostrils. Overall significant improvement noted but not completely resolved.

RESULTS
Clinical examination as documented above.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Perioral dermatitis and rosacea, including ocular rosacea. Continue doxycycline twice daily until rash is completely resolved, then continue once daily for one additional week before stopping. Initiate tacrolimus ointment (calcineurin inhibitor, not a steroid) applied to affected rash areas on face twice daily until resolved. Patient counseled that tacrolimus may cause mild tingling, needle-like sensation, or flushing for a few seconds after application, which is not an allergic reaction. Continue sulfacetamide wash; patient may reduce to once daily to avoid over-drying if needed. Continue metro cream. Add moisturizer such as vanicream or petroleum jelly as needed. Provided samples of moisturizer. Patient counseled to avoid steroids on face, maintain sun protection, and avoid new products until discussed with physician. Once rash resolves, discontinue tacrolimus but continue doxycycline for one additional week. Can continue face wash and metro cream long-term. If mild flare occurs, may try tacrolimus alone for a couple of days; if insufficient, restart doxycycline. If rash worsens, patient to contact office or send MyChart message. Gentle eyelid cleansing once daily with gentle cleanser such as vanicream. Use Bruder mask as needed. Cancelled elidel prescription and discontinued clindamycin from medication list. Tacrolimus ointment prescription sent to pharmacy with patient assistance for cost considerations. Follow-up appointment scheduled in approximately 4 weeks.
